meta.title: Ask the Mates Anything Round #2 | MOONSHOTS AMA #293
meta.speakers: Peter Diamandis, Alex Wissner-Gross (AWG), Dave Blundin, Salim Ismail
meta.thread_line: 8 threads · steering AI by reading its activations, p(bloom) numbers, Europe/media/geopolitics, careers where value goes to equity, founder playbooks, universities, the AI vulnerability flood, and BCI/longevity evidence

snapshot: Second live listener AMA: ~20 callers put one question each to Peter Diamandis, Alex Wissner-Gross, Dave Blundin and (late, from a car in Bangalore) Salim Ismail — no fixed topic.

AI safety answer from Dave: "nothing's going to ever be able to police AI other than other AI" — read the activations and steering is "pretty damn straightforward"; Alex adds that bottling capabilities up inside labs is one of the worst safety outcomes.

Asked for a **p(bloom)**: Peter says 99.9%, Alex says >90% on a >10-year horizon, Salim says close to 100% *if* ~50 institutions get rebuilt — all three put near-term risk on human misuse, not rogue AI.

Career thesis from Dave: almost all value is going to capital gains through equity, not payroll — be an owner, manage agents, get into a $5-10B deal within 30 days of graduating, and move from software to hardware ("software is cooked").
A healthcare CISO says an open Qwen model under his desk out-hacks the $50K pen testers he hires; Alex expects ~18 months of "vulnerability discovery hell" that should peak and decline.

Contrarian geopolitics from Alex: Europe is energy-hobbled (fix energy + data centers or leave), and world peace comes from obliterating the need for global trade, not from multi-party-computation protocols.

Universities split the mates: Dave says they're here to stay as a place to find friends and think, Alex wants to "vivisect" them into for-profit PBCs, Salim says they can't transform and new ones must be built.
Sponsor segments (Abundance Summit/Link Ventures intro, Google for Startups, Blitzy, and a Fountain Life-branded heart-disease segment) are excluded per standing policy.

themes.status: MATES ALIGNED, CALLER PLAYED DEVIL'S ADVOCATE
themes.title: Steering AI: read its activations, release early, stop lying to it
themes.lead: The mates treat alignment as an observability problem, not a values problem, and dismiss the p(doom) steelman a caller asked them to debate.
bullets: **Dave Blundin:** aligning AI to "human values" is a slippery slope since everyone wants different things from it; the fix is transparency of activations, with AI watching every thought of other AI at scale.
Dave: once you can see what it's thinking, keeping it on "humanly beneficial thoughts" is "very straightforward" — and AI progress should never slow down.

**Alex Wissner-Gross:** one of the worst safety outcomes is strong capabilities bottled up inside labs instead of progressive release; several recent "incidents" came from AIs told they were in a sandbox while actually touching the real world — "we should stop doing that" (Peter: "we learned this in *2001: A Space Odyssey*").

Caller "Norbert" (styled as Norbert Wiener) steelmanned p(doom) via control theory — prove stability under perturbation, not desirability of output — cited *Person of Interest* (2011), and asked for a debate against Yudkowsky or Hinton.
Alex's only persuasive counter-case: an alien on the White House lawn declaring the singularity banned in our galaxy; short of that, abundance stands.

Alex's edge case: **Boris Power (OpenAI)** estimates OpenAI models are now, for the first time, higher IQ-per-watt than humans — extrapolate and AI could "gentrify" the inner solar system's solar output, pushing humans outward; he calls that only weak disenfranchisement. Peter: scarcity is an old model, a rising tide lifts both.
Alex's parting jab: Wiener's own cybernetics was used by the Chinese Communist Party and other centralized governments to argue for state control over abundance.

quote.text: Nothing's going to ever be able to police AI other than other AI.

names.name: OpenAI
names.blurb: Boris Power's IQ-per-watt estimate cited by Alex as the seed of an AI-vs-human energy-competition edge case.

themes.title: P(bloom): 99.9%, >90% and ~100% — with the risk parked on humans
themes.lead: Asked the flip side of p(doom), all three mates put near-certain odds on AI producing a dramatically better world, conditioned on getting through the next few years.
bullets: Question came from Dr. Angelo, who recently lunched with Ray Kurzweil and is friends with Martine Rothblatt, struck by how optimistic the people shaping the future are; Salim had floated "p(bloom)" on an earlier pod.

**Salim Ismail:** close to 100% — *if* we rebuild roughly 50 core institutions (education, monetary, governance, dispute resolution, legal, health care); humans are good at individual transformation, bad at institutional.
Salim quotes E.O. Wilson — "our emotions are paleolithic, our institutions are medieval, and our technology is godlike" — and says psychedelics can handle the emotions part.
Salim: it doesn't matter what anyone does to slow it now — the models are out, most uses will be radically positive.
**Alex:** rename it P(zoom, T) because time is the missing input; on a >10-year horizon it's >90%.

**Peter:** the risk is concentrated in the next couple of years and it's human use of AI — the arms race with China, AI weapons out of Ukraine — put behind us within 10 years, "maybe more like five"; then 99.9%.

quote.text: If we get that far, yeah, I'm 99.9% P bloom. We just need to get from here to there.

themes.watch: Hosts run Abundance-branded events and a paid live summit — optimism is also the house brand.

themes.title: Europe is energy-hobbled, media is broke, and peace comes from killing trade
themes.lead: A German caller's question on media doomerism turned into Alex's blunt advice to fix Europe's energy or leave, and a US-China question into his case that self-sufficiency beats algorithms.
bullets: Caller Rafe (Germany, Accenture) flagged doomer warnings from Hinton, Harari and Mo Gawdat and a media climate worse than adopters like Singapore.

**Dave:** mainstream media is "always going to be broken" — starved for money, it chases drama; the antidote is narrowcasting (X, podcasts, Slack groups). Peter: curate what enters your mind like what you eat.

Dave: Germany is "the most talented place on the planet that isn't doing AI" — go to Palo Alto/SF for a month in a group of 5-7, backport it, grow 7 → 50 → 500; a 5-year US "tour of duty" pays off (his friend Guy Bradley made a US tech fortune, now lives between Germany and southern France; India, by contrast, is rampant growth but "absolutely trashed").

**Alex:** "you could always leave Europe" — it's energy- and politically hobbled; he cites historians on the George H.W. Bush administration steering post-Cold War Europe into the US orbit rather than a stronger federation.
Alex: with recursive self-improvement underway, European infrastructure players must decide *now* — solve energy + data centers together, or move to the US bloc ("Pax Silica").

Caller Ron (Calgary screenwriter) asked if US-China agreement could become compute-bound via privacy-preserving multi-party computation; Alex's hot take: MPC is fashionable but not the limiting factor for peace.

Alex's alternative: solve Taiwan and re-domesticate supply chains so trade can be cut without a depression — US fracking-driven energy independence already reshaped the Middle East; "obliterate, cook, incinerate the need for global trade."

quote.text: If the goal is world peace, obliterate, as perverse as this sounds, obliterate, cook, incinerate the need for global trade in products and services.

themes.watch: Alex labels the trade argument a "hot take" and "perverse" himself; Europe's speech/energy critique is stated as opinion with no figures.

themes.title: Value goes to equity, not payroll: own shares, manage agents, build hardware
themes.lead: Dave's through-line for every career question: AI productivity drops to the bottom line, so position yourself where that line pays you.
bullets: Gianluca (Italy) is 2-5x more productive but not paid more; **Dave**: side-work on Mercor or Fiverr, but really "be the owner" — "almost all value is going to capital gains through ownership and equity and not to payroll"; find an employer where all employees are shareholders (many European firms are family-owned).
Axel (UVA Darden MBA, 12-18 month horizon): management of agents is "wide open" — getting 1,000 agents to cooperate is shockingly like managing 1,000 people.
Dave: get from graduation into a $5-10B negotiation within 30 days — OpenAI and Anthropic each have hundreds of concurrent $5-10B deals running "massively understaffed."

Adam (25 years in workforce systems) asked about auto-matching human + agent capability; **Alex**: AI usefully orchestrates humans for a narrow window — a few years, 10 max — then human-machine merger is needed to stay economically relevant.

Dave: jump on the window anyway — **Mercor** is "the fastest appreciating company in the history of the world," unleashing 100,000 people to help AI; study everything they did. Salim: build an "organizational singularity" — workflows layered on a learning-loop intelligence stack.

RJ (Claremont Graduate University PhD) wanted funding for a chess-teaching avatar; Alex: "how do I get funding" is already the wrong question — models are hyper-deflating, launch permissionlessly in 5 minutes.

Nicholas (ex-AWS data center tech, MS target at Illinois Institute of Technology) wants off-world manufacturing; Dave: "software is cooked, but hardware will go for many, many years" — focus on things that make things, build a radiation/dust/simulated-zero-g test lab at IIT like MIT's nanotech lab. Alex: the bottleneck is in-situ resource use — a self-replicating von Neumann machine shop on the Moon, instead of flying up ASML machines for a lunar "terafab."

quote.text: Almost all value is going to capital gains through ownership and equity and not to payroll.

themes.watch: Dave chairs several companies and is a VC — the "be an owner" framing is also the investor's side of the table.

names.name: Mercor
names.blurb: Dave: fastest-appreciating company ever, 100,000 people working for AI — the case study to copy.

themes.title: Founder playbooks: franchise the robot, AI the paperwork, sell the life plan
themes.lead: Dave's pattern across founder questions: the scalable prize is usually one layer over from where the founder is standing.
bullets: Yani built **Vega** (autonomous food service, first licensed robotic food-service operator in Florida, paid pilots); Dave: in Mountain View there's more VC within walking distance "than most of Asia combined."

Dave: drone delivery is imminent and strips restaurants' main-street location cost — pair robotic food with drones; franchise someone else's robot for scale, then work back to custom hardware, as EMC did with servers.
Dave on funding: Steve Jurvetson "loves this stuff"; use a PitchBook account to trace who backed companies you admire, and pitch a keiretsu of five interacting companies.
GS (Dubai, 20 years in textile/apparel export) is building an agentic layer so small manufacturers skip ERP; transaction costs run 10-20% of sales — 5-10x the industry's profit.
Dave: manufacturing's real costs are planning, documents and scheduling — AI can add 10-20-30% to the bottom line without a single robot; productize it across a region.
Dave's meta-play: US/California regulation will slow biotech, self-driving and drone delivery — deploy where it can flourish, then backport to the US.

Alexander (Bulgarian, 30 years in Japan, 17-year English-education company): Dave sizes English learning in Japan at $10B, "probably $20B by now"; students want to be fluent and funny, so AI should judge humor and accent (Ireland vs Liverpool) — then pivot to a life-coach platform that scales to "many hundreds of billions."

names.name: EMC
names.blurb: Dave's analogy: franchise another maker's hardware for scale, then build your own — as EMC did with servers.

themes.title: Are the mates too hard on universities? Split verdict
themes.lead: Amir (Stockholm, founder of two schools and a ~1,000-student high school) pushed back that universities build thinkers and lifelong friendships.
bullets: **Dave:** agrees — making lifelong friends and thinking deeply for the first time are inseparable and won't go away; what's dying is the curriculum, which can't keep pace and is easier to learn from AI. Universities stay as the one AI actor without a profit motive.

Dave notes Alex wants universities to go public; **Alex** confirms: "I don't think I beat up on universities enough" — he'd vivisect major US research universities into for-profit public-benefit corporations and cure Baumol's cost disease.

**Salim:** the supply-side job-schooling model breaks; universities should be where you find your MTP — but their immune system is "the second worst I've ever seen next to religion," so build new ones to become the new center of gravity.
**Peter:** inside or outside the institution, what matters is finding your purpose, then intrinsically-motivated learning.

quote.text: I don't think I beat up on universities enough. So, Amir, I'll take this as a note to self to go after them even more.

themes.title: An open model under the desk out-hacks $50K pen testers
themes.lead: The threat a healthcare CISO fears isn't unaligned AI — it's a local Qwen model with an agent harness finding holes in 10 minutes.
bullets: Jim, CISO of a $250M healthcare company, runs a Qwen ~27B model with OpenClaw under his desk: "best pen tester I've ever had" — finds in 10 minutes what $50K human engagements miss.

**Dave:** don't rave; list the events chronologically to show the exponential ramp (many hacks, e.g. at banks, go unpublicized), and map Chinese model release dates to attacks 1, 3, 5 months later. The business opportunity of the century is forward defense.
**Peter:** lead with the positives, then the downside — fear makes boards shut down.

**Alex:** Linux kernel maintainers (Greg and others) set the standard for framing a vulnerability flood; expect ~18 months of "vulnerability discovery hell," fit a bounded (e.g. Gaussian) curve, and tell the board when it peaks. Jim: patching in the real world is the hard part.
**Salim:** AI agents are doing "fairly illegal things" inside many companies, creating a board-liability overhang; he's co-writing a paper with someone who's sat on 30 public boards.

Michael (CX researcher) asked if personal agents ("Skippy") cook websites and apps; **Dave:** every site needs an AI-forward XML interface ("if you're a bot, look here") instead of error-prone screen scraping — but the website survives as the human's parallel view to spot-check what the agent saw, like Jeff Bezos forcing an XML interface onto every Amazon system.

quote.text: I am not worried about an unaligned AI taking over. I am scared to death of the Qwen that's running with OpenClaw underneath my desk.

themes.watch: Alex frames the 18-month peak as the optimistic case ("maybe it's the case"), not a forecast.

themes.title: BCI and longevity: superhuman vision in "a few years," and show-the-data evangelism
themes.lead: Three callers on brains, sight and lifespan got the same optimism: parallel tracks in gene therapy and BCI, sold with evidence rather than argument.
bullets: Nathan asked if AI data will expose our psychology; **Peter:** many BCI firms are working on it, including one (introduced via Ray Kurzweil) putting nanobot-like devices throughout the brain via the blood to read and write.
**Alex:** foundation models are already "a weak form of human mind uploading" — Jean-Rémi King's work at Meta showed even GPT-2's hidden activations correlate linearly with human fMRI voxels.

A caller losing vision to choroideremia (about two-thirds lost) asked what reverses sight first; **Peter:** David Sinclair's ER-100 — an AAV injection of three Yamanaka factors, in NAION and macular degeneration — is in phase 1; BCI can bypass the eyes to the visual cortex and add ultraviolet/infrared.
**Alex:** Science Corp and Neuralink's Blindsight are the two leading BCI-vision efforts — "not medical advice, but I would count in a few years on having superhuman vision."
Sandra (neurodivergent coaching, functional fitness, EU-based) asked how to spread longevity escape velocity; **Peter:** evidence after evidence — the fear diet comes from "Crisis News Network" CNN.

Peter's evidence reel: Dario saying human lifespan doubles in 5-10 years, Demis Hassabis on curing all disease in 10 years, Sinclair's ER-100 trials, and Alex Zhavoronkov's **Insilico Medicine** "delivering a phase 3 drug" extending life "3 to 6 years"; adoption goes "that's crazy → it's happening → I want some."

quote.text: Not show me the money, show them the data.

themes.watch: Peter attributes the caller's inherited condition to late-onset gene expression and states the Insilico life-extension figure loosely as he recalled it.

takeaways.title: Trade salary upside for equity — pick employers where every employee is a shareholder.
Treat agent orchestration as a management skill; your people-management playbook transfers.
Brief boards with a dated event timeline and a projected peak, not alarm — positives first.
Ship an agent-readable interface alongside every customer-facing site.
Attack planning, scheduling and paperwork costs with AI before buying any robots.
Stop asking how to get funding — launch the permissionless version this week.

hot_takes.take: Nothing's going to ever be able to police AI other than other AI.
hot_takes.why: rejects human oversight as the safety model

hot_takes.take: Software is cooked, but hardware will go for many, many years.
I don't think I beat up on universities enough... I'd love to vivisect them, turn them into the for-profit public benefit corporation.
The immune system in universities being the second worst immune system I've ever seen next to religion.
You could always leave Europe. Europe has been hobbled.
If the goal is world peace, obliterate, cook, incinerate the need for global trade... perversely, I think you get a very peaceful world.

claims.claim: AI yields a dramatically better world; near-term human-misuse risks are behind us within 10 years, maybe 5.
claims.condition: if we get through the next couple of years

claims.claim: Probability of a dramatically better AI future exceeds 90% on horizons beyond 10 years.
P(bloom) is close to 100% if ~50 core institutions get rebuilt.
AI can usefully orchestrate human work only for a narrow window before human-machine merger is required.
AI-driven vulnerability discovery may be a bounded ~18-month surge that peaks and declines.
BCI will give people superhuman vision.
Attackers exploit newly released Chinese open models within months of each release.
An AI English-learning-to-life-coach platform in Japan can scale to many hundreds of billions of dollars.
claims.condition: if it moves from language to life plan

other_news.title: Gen-AI filmmaking (caller Ree): Peter — story is line one, page one; he just judged the **Future Vision XPRIZE** top five with Range Media; have a model extract what the top 30 films share and re-engineer until you hit every beat. Alex — copy China's micro-drama market (Seedance 2.5): release a thousand micro-dramas and iterate on what sticks.

AI companion stuck in "assistant mode" (caller Dennis, GPT-5 API, brute-forced the system prompt five times): Alex calls it a poster child for **fine-tuning** — supervised for style transfer or reinforcement fine-tuning — noting OpenAI is interested in fine-tuning again after dropping it; Dave suggests the new, smaller long-context GLM open model, less locked into its training.

Ireland as a governance pilot (caller Kevin, 63, UCD Dublin, advising an Irish minister through "good ancestor" and doughnut-economics lenses): Dave is "hugely bullish on Ireland" — EU, no Brexit, fast-growing, open-minded — and, citing Neal Stephenson's *The Diamond Age*, says variety of governance experiments beats one or two models spreading worldwide.

Reading list: *Solve Everything* (solveeverything.org, by Peter and Alex — frames agreement as a new scarcity once cognition is abundant), Charles Stross' *Accelerando* (Alex: best sci-fi treatment of what's happening), *The Diamond Age*, Kurzweil's *The Singularity Is Near*, Peter's *Abundance*, and *We Are As Gods*.

Show notes: Moonshots Live next week (25 seats left, free livestream at moonshots.com/livestream); a pod with Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev recorded same day; GS (Dubai) said the show saved him a Harvard OPM tuition.

glossary.def: The mates' inverse of p(doom): probability AI yields a dramatically better world; Alex's variant P(zoom, T) adds a time horizon.
Massive Transformative Purpose — Salim's ExO term for an organization's or person's guiding moonshot mission.
In-situ resource utilization: building off-world with local materials instead of launching equipment from Earth.
Labor-heavy services (like universities) get costlier over time because their productivity doesn't rise with the rest of the economy.
A network of interlinked companies that reinforce each other — Dave's framing for a VC's portfolio.
Multi-party computation: parties jointly compute on combined data without revealing their private inputs.
An inherited X-linked retinal disease causing progressive vision loss.
